extracted.intended_audience: research community and public stakeholders (investigators, administrators, policymakers) interested in NIH extramural funding data
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and explanation of NIH extramural grant investment metrics (counts, amounts, success rates, averages) for fiscal year comparisons, including data inclusion/exclusion rules and caveats. Intended to communicate FY2023–FY2025 trends and data definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Awards (All Extramural Research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of all extramural research awards (competing and non-competing, excluding R&D contracts) for the fiscal year (Table 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an absolute number by fiscal year (e.g., 55,394 awards in FY2025). Applies to extramural grants and other included award types; excludes R&D contracts. Use this metric to track changes in award volume year-to-year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Amount (All Extramural Research, in billions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total dollar amount NIH awarded for extramural research (competing and non-competing grants) during the fiscal year (Table 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in billions of dollars (e.g., $35.30B in FY2025). Note that the NIH's full appropriation also funds R&D contracts, intramural research, administrative support, etc., which are not included here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of RPG Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of research project grant (RPG) applications submitted in the fiscal year (Table 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an annual count (e.g., 62,592 in FY2025). This input metric is used with award counts to compute success rates and to assess demand for investigator-initiated research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of New or Renewal (Competing) RPG Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of new or renewal (competing) RPG awards made in the fiscal year (Table 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an annual count (e.g., 8,161 in FY2025). Changes in this number (declines or increases) directly affect calculated success rates and reflect NIH award activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success Rate of RPG Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of RPG applications that received awards in the fiscal year (Table 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a percentage (e.g., 13.0% in FY2025). The page notes the success rate declined because of a decrease in the number of awards combined with an increase in applications. Use caution interpreting year-to-year changes because they can be influenced by award timing, forward funding, and other procedural factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average Size of RPGs
rubrics_metrics.description: Average dollar amount per RPG award in the fiscal year (Table 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a mean award size (e.g., $675,426 in FY2025). The page notes average cost per award increased and that forward funding (awards spread over future years) likely affected average award size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Amount of NIH Funding to RPGs (competing and non-competing, in billions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total dollars NIH allocated to RPGs (both competing and non-competing) during the fiscal year (Table 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in billions (e.g., $26.503B in FY2025). Use this to track portion of NIH extramural funding directed to RPGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of R01-equivalent Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of R01-equivalent grant applications submitted in the fiscal year (Table 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an annual count (e.g., 42,022 in FY2025). R01-equivalents comprise the majority of RPGs and are tracked separately to show trends in the traditional investigator-initiated award category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of New or Renewal (Competing) R01-equivalent Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of new or renewal (competing) R01-equivalent awards made in the fiscal year (Table 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an annual count (e.g., 5,471 in FY2025). Declines in this number affect R01-equivalent success rates and reflect funding activity for this award class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success Rates for R01-equivalent Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of R01-equivalent applications that received awards in the fiscal year (Table 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a percentage (e.g., 13.0% in FY2025). The page highlights a substantial year-to-year decline; interpret changes alongside application volume and award-count changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average Size of R01-equivalent Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Average dollar amount per R01-equivalent award in the fiscal year (Table 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a mean award size (e.g., $664,005 in FY2025). Note that forward funding and changes in award mix can affect averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Amount of NIH Funding to R01-equivalents (competing and non-competing, in billions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total dollars NIH allocated to R01-equivalent awards during the fiscal year (Table 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in billions (e.g., $20.840B in FY2025). Use this to assess how much funding is concentrated in R01-equivalent mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Inclusion/Exclusion Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines which financial instruments are counted in the reported grant data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monies for grants and Other Transaction awards are included while research and development (R&D) contracts are excluded. Previous-year spending related to special appropriations for coronavirus are excluded from comparisons unless otherwise specified (these can be found via RePORTER). These rules are critical when comparing across years or datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: Forward Funding and Timing Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation that changes in award counts and average award size may be affected by awards being forward funded and by timing differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes fewer new awards but higher average cost per award in FY2025, likely influenced by more awards being forward funded. Users interpreting trends should account for timing/forward-funding effects rather than assuming changes reflect solely programmatic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Transparency in Data Reporting (Gold Standard Science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy/communicative standard that NIH will provide transparent data reporting to maintain public confidence and enable community planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH commits to continuing to provide detailed funding data (FY-by-FY) so the research community can plan and the public can understand where investments are going; transparency is presented as part of the 'Gold Standard Science' commitment.
